You are building ONE small Python script: the registry handler that turns an approved identity card into a verified state write. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Use ONLY fictional names/emails in tests (like 'Rosa Marchetti <rosa@fictionalpractice.invalid>'). Never copy real guest data from the repo into tests.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES (create both):
  1. scripts/apply_identity_approve.py
  2. tests/test_apply_identity_approve.py
Touching any other tracked file fails the check.

## Why this matters

The podcast guest funnel writes and notifies but does not RESOLVE: when the owner approves a proposed guest address, nothing executes. This handler is the execution end of the first resolution slice: kernel dispatch (already built, /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/factory/approve_dispatch.py — READ IT to match its handler contract) will invoke your script with an approved decision payload; your job is to write the address into candidate state with provenance, verified, or refuse loudly.

## SHARED SLICE CONTRACT (three lanes build to this; deviation breaks the seam)

All state lives under a root directory R (CLI flag --root, REQUIRED here):
  R/episodes/CANDIDATE-INBOX.json            {"candidates": [{"name": str, "email": str|null, ...}]}
  R/episodes/_loop_state/approve-ledger.jsonl / approve-decisions.jsonl / approve-receipts.jsonl / approve-registry.json
Ledger row: {"card_identifier", "kind": "identity-approve", "packet_text": canonical JSON of the proposal (json.dumps(p, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)), "row_hash": sha256 hexdigest of packet_text, "status": "open"|"decided:approve"|"decided:skip", "ts": ISO-8601 UTC}
Proposal packet fields: {"alias", "name", "channel", "value", "evidence", "confidence", "source"} — value is the proposed address, name is the candidate's name.
Decision row: {"card_identifier", "decision": "approve"|"skip", "kind": "identity-approve", "row_hash", "ts"}

## Your handler's exact behavior

Invocation: python3 scripts/apply_identity_approve.py --root R. The kernel passes the decision payload as canonical JSON on STDIN; the payload includes "approved_row" = the full open ledger row (with packet_text). Parse the proposal from approved_row.packet_text.

1. Load R/episodes/CANDIDATE-INBOX.json. Find the candidate whose name matches the proposal name case-insensitively after whitespace normalization. Not found → print a one-line reason to stderr, exit 4, write NOTHING.
2. If the candidate already has a non-null email DIFFERENT from the proposal value → conflict: print reason to stderr, exit 5, write NOTHING (never silently overwrite). Same email already present → idempotent success: exit 0 without rewriting.
3. Otherwise set email = proposal value and add provenance fields on the candidate: identity_source, identity_channel, identity_evidence, identity_confidence (from the packet), approved_via = card_identifier, decision_hash if present in the payload, approved_at = now ISO-8601 UTC. Preserve every other candidate and field byte-for-byte (load/dump with json, indent 1 to match the existing file style, ensure_ascii=False).
4. Re-read the file after writing and verify the email landed; only then print a one-line receipt JSON to stdout ({"written": name, "channel", "value", "card": card_identifier}) and exit 0. Failed verify → exit 6.
5. Malformed stdin/missing fields → exit 2 with reason on stderr. Never raise an unhandled traceback for bad input.

## tests/test_apply_identity_approve.py (pytest, tmp_path roots, fictional data)

Cover at least: successful write with all provenance fields + re-read verification; not-found refusal (exit 4, file unchanged); conflict refusal (exit 5, file unchanged); idempotent same-email success; malformed stdin (exit 2); other candidates untouched byte-for-byte. Drive the script as a subprocess with real stdin, the way the kernel will.

## Run until green

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_apply_identity_approve.py -q
tasks.check: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_apply_identity_approve.py -q && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-card-slice/checks/export_patch.py --worktree "$PWD" --patch /mnt/d_drive/ringer-work/one-card-slice-s1/s1-handler.patch --owned scripts/apply_identity_approve.py --owned tests/test_apply_identity_approve.py
tasks.verified: Executes the handler's own pytest suite (subprocess-driven with real stdin: verified write with provenance, not-found and conflict refusals leave the file unchanged, idempotent replay, malformed input) and exports the patch only if no out-of-scope file changed.

You are building ONE small Python script: the card creator that turns the newest identity proposal into ONE owner-approval card packet. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Use ONLY fictional names/emails in tests. Never copy real guest data from the repo into tests.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES (create both):
  1. scripts/identity_card.py
  2. tests/test_identity_card.py
Touching any other tracked file fails the check.

## Why this matters

The loop proposes guest addresses (episodes/_loop_receipts/identity-proposals-*.json) but nothing asks the owner. This script creates exactly ONE approval card per open question — never a card flood — and its ledger row is what the kernel later binds the approval receipt to.

## SHARED SLICE CONTRACT (three lanes build to this; deviation breaks the seam)

All state lives under a root directory R (CLI flag --root, default '.'):
  R/episodes/_loop_receipts/identity-proposals-YYYYMMDD.json   {"schema": "identity-proposals/v1", "proposals": [{"alias", "name", "channel", "value", "evidence", "confidence", "source"}], ...}
  R/episodes/CANDIDATE-INBOX.json                              {"candidates": [{"name": str, "email": str|null, "fit_score": int, ...}]}
  R/episodes/_loop_state/approve-ledger.jsonl                  (append-only JSONL)
  R/out/                                                        (generated card artifacts)
Ledger row you append: {"card_identifier", "kind": "identity-approve", "packet_text": canonical JSON of the chosen proposal (json.dumps(p, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)), "row_hash": sha256 hexdigest of packet_text, "status": "open", "ts": ISO-8601 UTC}

## Your script's exact behavior

Invocation: python3 scripts/identity_card.py --root R [--offline] [--post]

1. ONE-CARD RULE: read the ledger (may be absent). If any identity-approve row's latest status for its card_identifier is "open", print that row's card_identifier and exit 0 WITHOUT creating anything (idempotent re-run).
2. Load the NEWEST identity-proposals-*.json by filename date. Load CANDIDATE-INBOX.json. Select exactly ONE proposal: candidates whose inbox entry (name matched case-insensitively, whitespace-normalized) has email null or missing; among those pick highest proposal confidence, tie-break higher inbox fit_score, then alias ascending. No eligible proposal → print '{"selected": null}' and exit 3, writing nothing.
3. Compute packet_text + row_hash. card_identifier: in --offline mode use 'OFFLINE-' + row_hash[:12]. With --post, create a REAL Linear card via subprocess: python3 /home/ankit114/scripts/linear_control_ticket.py --agent cli-claude-code-linux --kind identity-approve --dispatch-mode manual --source podcast:identity-card --dedupe-key <row_hash> --title 'Guest identity approval: <name>' --body <the body you generated> — READ that script first to learn its stdout shape and parse the created issue identifier (e.g. ANK-123) from it; creation failure → exit 7 with stderr reason, append NO ledger row (a card that does not exist must never be in the ledger).
4. Write R/out/identity-card-body.md. It MUST lead with a '## YOUR MOVE (10 seconds)' block: one plain-English line saying what this is (approve this address for this guest so outreach can proceed), the exact reply strings — APPROVE, SKIP, or FIX: <notes> — and a one-line recommendation with the confidence number. Then a details section: name, channel, proposed address, evidence, confidence, source, alias, row_hash. No em dashes; short lines; ELI5 first.
5. Write R/out/identity-card-comment.md: first line exactly 'AGENT UPDATE: proposed identity for approval' then the FULL payload (name, channel, address, evidence, confidence, source) — the newest comment must BE the payload under review.
6. Write R/out/identity-card-doorbell.txt: a 2-3 line Telegram doorbell text — 'PODCAST IDENTITY — YOUR MOVE: <name>' + the card identifier + the one-line ask. (Sending is NOT your job; another component delivers it.)
7. Append the ledger row LAST, only after every artifact above succeeded. Print a one-line JSON receipt to stdout: {"card_identifier", "row_hash", "name"}.

## tests/test_identity_card.py (pytest, tmp_path roots, fictional data)

Cover at least: selection rule (null-email candidate wins over already-resolved higher-confidence one; confidence then fit_score tie-breaks); one-card idempotence (second run creates nothing new); no-eligible exit 3; ledger row field completeness and canonical row_hash (recompute sha256 in the test); YOUR MOVE block leads the body and contains APPROVE/SKIP and the address; comment first line marker; doorbell mentions the name and card identifier; ledger written last (simulate body-write failure via a read-only out dir → no ledger row). Offline mode only in tests; never call the real Linear script.

## Run until green

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_identity_card.py -q
tasks.check: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_identity_card.py -q && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-card-slice/checks/export_patch.py --worktree "$PWD" --patch /mnt/d_drive/ringer-work/one-card-slice-s1/s1-card.patch --owned scripts/identity_card.py --owned tests/test_identity_card.py
tasks.verified: Executes the creator's pytest suite (selection rule with tie-breaks, one-open-card idempotence, no-eligible no-op, canonical row_hash recomputed independently, YOUR MOVE body contract, payload-comment marker, doorbell content, ledger-written-last ordering) and exports the patch only if no out-of-scope file changed.

tasks.spec:
You are building ONE small Python script: the reply listener that turns a HUMAN approval on an identity card into an executed kernel dispatch and a closed card. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Use ONLY fictional names/emails in tests. Never copy real guest data from the repo into tests.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES (create both):
  1. scripts/identity_card_listen.py
  2. tests/test_identity_card_listen.py
Touching any other tracked file fails the check.

## Why this matters

Owner rule: a card that asks a question MUST have a listener that pulls the reply back and applies it — a card nobody listens to is a broken promise. Approval grammar is HUMAN-ONLY: an agent comment must NEVER count as an approval. Your listener is what makes an APPROVE actually EXECUTE (via the already-built kernel) instead of rotting in a comment thread.

## SHARED SLICE CONTRACT (three lanes build to this; deviation breaks the seam)

All state lives under a root directory R (CLI flag --root, default '.'):
  R/episodes/_loop_state/approve-ledger.jsonl / approve-decisions.jsonl / approve-receipts.jsonl / approve-registry.json
  R/out/
Ledger row: {"card_identifier", "kind": "identity-approve", "packet_text": canonical proposal JSON, "row_hash": sha256 of packet_text, "status": "open"|"decided:approve"|"decided:skip", "ts"} — the LATEST row per card_identifier wins.
Decision row you append: {"card_identifier", "decision": "approve"|"skip", "kind": "identity-approve", "row_hash", "ts"} (add "notes": str for FIX).
Comments shape (Linear-like, oldest to newest): [{"body": str, "user": {"name": str, "displayName": str}}]
Kernel (READ IT FIRST — /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/factory/approve_dispatch.py): invoke as [sys.executable, that path, "--ledger", ..., "--decisions", ..., "--receipts", ..., "--registry", ..., "--apply", "--json"], parse the JSON report; the dispatch SUCCEEDED iff failed == 0 and (dispatched >= 1 or skipped_receipted >= 1). skipped_receipted means an earlier run already executed this decision — that is replay success, not failure.

## Your script's exact behavior

Invocation: python3 scripts/identity_card_listen.py --root R --comments-file F [--offline]
(--comments-file is REQUIRED in this round; a future round adds live Linear fetching.)

1. Find the latest identity-approve ledger row whose latest status is "open". None → print '{"open": null}' exit 0 (nothing to listen for).
2. Read the comments file. Find the FIRST comment that is a HUMAN decision:
   - author check: user.name and user.displayName must NOT start (case-insensitive) with any of: 'agent', 'cli-', 'hermes', 'vpam', 'codex', 'claude', 'qa'.
   - body first line must be exactly 'APPROVE' or exactly 'SKIP', or be 'FIX' or start with 'FIX:'.
   - a comment whose first line starts with an agent/QA marker ('AGENT ', 'QA REVIEW:') NEVER counts, whatever the author. The word APPROVE appearing anywhere later in a body never counts; ONLY the first line decides.
3. No human decision → print '{"decision": null}' exit 0. FIX is neither approve nor skip: append NOTHING to decisions, write R/out/identity-card-fix.md containing the FIX notes (full comment body), print '{"decision": "fix"}', exit 0; the card stays open awaiting a later APPROVE or SKIP.
4. APPROVE or SKIP → append the decision row, then append a ledger row {same card_identifier, kind, row_hash, packet_text, "status": "decided:approve"|"decided:skip", "ts"}. IMPORTANT: the kernel requires the decided ledger row's status to start with 'decided:approve' and binds by row_hash + a decision row with decision == 'approve'.
5. On SKIP: write R/out/identity-card-close.md, first line 'AGENT DONE: identity skipped by owner', include card_identifier; exit 0. No kernel call.
6. On APPROVE: run the kernel exactly as specified above with R's four state paths. Success (per the rule above) → write R/out/identity-card-close.md, first line 'AGENT DONE: identity executed', then the receipt row JSON (read the LAST line of approve-receipts.jsonl) and the line 'OPEN_ENGINE_STATE: Agent Done'; exit 0. Kernel failure or missing receipt → write NOTHING to out/, print the kernel report to stderr, exit 8 — a card must NEVER close without an execution receipt.
7. Replay safety: running the listener again with the same inputs must not append duplicate decision rows (skip appending if an identical decision for that card_identifier + row_hash already exists), must treat kernel skipped_receipted as success, and must leave exactly one receipt.
8. Never raise an unhandled traceback for malformed comments/ledger; refuse with exit 2 and a stderr reason.

## tests/test_identity_card_listen.py (pytest, tmp_path roots, fictional data)

Build real fixture roots (ledger with an open row whose packet_text/row_hash you compute canonically; registry pointing at a tiny fake handler script your test writes into tmp_path that appends a marker file and exits 0 — do NOT depend on the real handler, it is another lane). Cover at least: human APPROVE executes (decision row, decided ledger row, kernel receipt exists, close file with 'AGENT DONE:' first line); agent-authored 'APPROVE' body is ignored (author check) and 'AGENT UPDATE:' marker bodies are ignored; APPROVE mentioned mid-body is ignored; SKIP path (no kernel call, close file says skipped); FIX path (fix file written, no decision row, no close); replay run appends no duplicates and reports success via skipped_receipted; kernel handler exiting nonzero → exit 8 and NO close file. Drive the script as a subprocess.

## Run until green

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_identity_card_listen.py -q
tasks.check: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_identity_card_listen.py -q && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-card-slice/checks/export_patch.py --worktree "$PWD" --patch /mnt/d_drive/ringer-work/one-card-slice-s1/s1-listener.patch --owned scripts/identity_card_listen.py --owned tests/test_identity_card_listen.py
tasks.verified: Executes the listener's pytest suite (human-only grammar incl. author + marker + first-line-only rules, APPROVE dispatches through the real kernel binary against a test registry handler and closes only on receipt, SKIP and FIX paths, replay appends nothing and counts skipped_receipted as success, handler failure exits 8 with no close file) and exports the patch only if no out-of-scope file changed.
